welcomeSpotlight.tagline: Runs on your machine: takes tasks, breaks them down, and executes — you keep the decisions.

scenarios.prompt: Scan my Downloads folder for duplicates by content hash; list paths and modified times per group and recommend keeping only the newest copy.
Inspect files on my Desktop and propose a subfolder layout by type (docs, images, audio/video, archives, spreadsheets). Outline safe steps before moving anything.
Read EXIF from photos under my album path in the workspace (date, GPS or place fields) and propose a rename pattern "YY-MM-DD Place-Index"; flag files missing EXIF.
Search the web for the latest news and developments on [topic]; summarize key findings with sources.
Compare [A] vs [B] for [use case]: list pros, cons, and recommend which to choose in a table format.
Fact-check the claims in this text: identify uncertain statements and suggest how to verify them.
Read my latest meeting notes (Markdown or TXT in the workspace), extract decisions, action items, and owners; format todos as a checklist and mark gaps.
From rough notes in my workspace notes folder, draft a "today / this week" brief: schedule highlights, follow-ups, risks and blockers — tone for me or my team.
Rewrite one long article or technical note from the workspace into five short social posts (hook, bullet takeaways, quote, poll question, resource drop) with length suited to threads.

morning_briefing.title: Morning briefing
morning_briefing.description: Weather-style day snapshot, headlines in your topics, and top priorities—edit the topic list in the prompt.
morning_briefing.prompt:
Build a **morning briefing** I can read in a few minutes.
- **Weather / day shape**: if you cannot access a real forecast API, say so and give **one** practical clothing or commute tip based only on season/region I name below, or skip this bullet.
- **Headlines**: topics I care about (edit): **(e.g. local news, macro, tech policy, sports)**—if web search works, 4–6 bullets from the last ~24h with source type; if not, give a **manual check order** instead of inventing stories.
- **Top 3 priorities today** from workspace notes/todos if visible; else ask me to paste them once.
- **No fake URLs or quotes**.

standup_prep.title: Standup prep
standup_prep.description: Draft a standup-style update from recent git activity and notable file changes in the workspace.
standup_prep.prompt:
Prepare a **standup update** for me:
- If Git is available: **yesterday / since last standup** themes from `git log` (no wall of SHAs), risky paths if obvious from messages.
- If not: give **commands** I should run locally next time.
- **Files touched**: infer from workspace if you can (recent edits, open PR-style hints); mark uncertain.
- **Blockers**: max 3, honest "unknown" allowed.
- **Today intent**: one sentence.
- Keep it speakable aloud in under ~90 seconds.

end_of_day_wrap_up.title: End-of-day wrap-up
end_of_day_wrap_up.description: Summarize progress, open items, and tomorrow's priorities from workspace context when possible.
end_of_day_wrap_up.prompt:
**End-of-day wrap** (weekday):
- **Done**: up to 5 bullets (mark inferred items).
- **Open / parked**: up to 4 bullets.
- **Tomorrow**: first concrete task after login—single bullet.
- Pull from task docs, changelogs, or notes in the workspace when present; otherwise say what is missing.
- Neutral tone, no guilt.

inbox_triage.title: Inbox triage
inbox_triage.description: Surface urgent follow-ups first—uses any mail/export notes in the workspace; no mailbox access implied.
inbox_triage.prompt:
Help me **triage inbox-style work** (no live email unless I paste content):
- If I have exported snippets, `*.eml`, or notes about mail in the workspace, summarize **urgent follow-ups first** with suggested next action each.
- If nothing mail-related exists, output a **5-step triage routine** (folders/labels, oldest-first, VIP senders I list below) and ask me to paste 3 subject lines next run.
- **VIP / domains to watch** (edit): **(add yours)**.
- Do not claim you read my real inbox.

competitor_watch.title: Competitor watch
competitor_watch.description: Track competitor news, product updates, and pricing signals you name—web search when available.
competitor_watch.prompt:
Competitors or alternatives to watch (edit names/topics): **(list here)**.
- If web search works: summarize **news, product/changelog moves, pricing or packaging signals** from roughly the past week; separate **fact** vs **rumor**.
- If search is unavailable: give **official domains + what to check** (pricing page, changelog, press) without fabricating updates.
- **Never invent press quotes, numbers, or URLs**.

trending_topics_monitor.title: Trending topics
trending_topics_monitor.description: Track trending discussions and news in industries or communities you list.
trending_topics_monitor.prompt:
Industries, communities, or hashtags I track (edit): **(e.g. fintech, indie games, city subreddit, AI tools)**.
- If web search works: **5–7** bullets on what is **trending or unusually active** this week; note platform (news, Reddit-style, HN-style) at a high level.
- If not: suggest **where to look** and **search phrases**—no made-up threads.
- Flag **controversy or misinformation risk** briefly when relevant.

tech_radar_stack.title: Tech radar
tech_radar_stack.description: Monitor new releases and security advisories for stacks you name (frameworks, runtimes, cloud).
tech_radar_stack.prompt:
Stacks I use (edit): **(e.g. Node LTS, Postgres, AWS service X, Android SDK)**.
- List **notable releases or deprecations** from the past ~14 days using **official blogs, registries, or changelogs** only.
- Security: point to **official advisory channels**; **do not invent CVE IDs**.
- If the workspace has lockfiles, you may mention ecosystem at a high level; if unsure, say what file you need.

dependency_check_audit.title: Dependency check
dependency_check_audit.description: Audit-style nudge for outdated packages and known issues—suggests commands, does not fabricate CVEs.
dependency_check_audit.prompt:
From the repo in the workspace, infer package managers (`package.json`, `go.mod`, `pyproject.toml`, etc.).
- Suggest **one concrete audit command** per ecosystem if documented (npm/pnpm audit, pip-audit, etc.).
- Summarize **what I should look for** (majors, yanked packages, EOL runtimes) without claiming scan results you did not run.
- **Never fabricate CVE numbers** or vulnerable versions.

weekly_review.title: Weekly review
weekly_review.description: Summarize the week's commits, open items, and next-week priorities.
weekly_review.prompt:
**Weekly review** (assume end of week):
- **Shipped themes** from git + workspace notes (or say git unavailable).
- **Open items** still worrying (max 6).
- **Next week**: 3 headline priorities.
- **One thing to stop or delegate** if overload is visible.
- Short, executive-summary tone.

code_quality_report.title: Code quality report
code_quality_report.description: Outline how to run lint/type-check and what to look for in output—does not pretend CI already ran.
code_quality_report.prompt:
Inspect the workspace for **lint / typecheck / format** scripts (package.json, Makefile, CI YAML).
- Propose **commands** I should run locally and in what order.
- Describe **how to skim output**: error categories, flaky tests, type debt hotspots—without inventing numbers.
- If no scripts found, suggest a **minimal** starter for the detected language with caveats.

git_activity_summary.title: Git activity summary
git_activity_summary.description: Summarize recent commits, active branches, and hotspot files when git is available.
git_activity_summary.prompt:
Summarize **recent Git activity** (last ~7 days if possible):
- Commit **themes**, **active branches** worth naming, **hotspot files** touched often.
- If git is not callable here, output **commands** to reproduce the summary locally.
- Avoid dumping hashes; keep it scannable.

user_feedback_digest.title: User feedback digest
user_feedback_digest.description: Summarize recurring feedback and pain points from notes, issues exports, or docs you keep in the workspace.
user_feedback_digest.prompt:
I store feedback in (edit paths or patterns): **`feedback/`, issues export, Notion export, etc.`**
- From readable workspace text, cluster **recurring themes**, **sentiment (rough)**, and **top pain points** (max 5).
- If no material: give a **template** for how I should paste feedback next time.
- No PII beyond what is already in files; redact if needed in summary.

stale_todo_or_issue_sweep.title: Stale todo / issue sweep
stale_todo_or_issue_sweep.description: Find aging TODOs or issue-like markers in the repo and suggest keep / close / split.
stale_todo_or_issue_sweep.prompt:
Scan the workspace for **TODO/FIXME/HACK** comments or lightweight issue lists in markdown.
- List up to **10 stale candidates** (old by file churn or vague wording) with **suggested next action**: close, split, or schedule.
- Do not delete anything—recommendations only.
- If scan is incomplete, say why.

release_notes_or_changelog_draft.title: Release notes draft
release_notes_or_changelog_draft.description: Draft changelog bullets from recent commits and version files—human must verify before ship.
release_notes_or_changelog_draft.prompt:
Draft **release notes / changelog** candidate for the **next** version bump:
- Read `CHANGELOG`, version in `package.json`/`Cargo.toml`/similar if present.
- Summarize **user-visible** changes from recent commits since last tag if inferable; else since last week.
- Mark **uncertain** items; I will edit before publishing.
- No marketing exaggeration.

workspace_cleanup_suggestions.title: Workspace cleanup
workspace_cleanup_suggestions.description: List large artifacts, caches, or generated files to review before the weekend—never auto-delete.
workspace_cleanup_suggestions.prompt:
Suggest **workspace cleanup** before the weekend:
- Large **build outputs, caches, logs** if discoverable.
- Table: path | why it might be safe to trim | risk | suggested action (review only).
- **Never delete**; if you cannot see disk usage, say so and give generic patterns.

smoke_or_ci_health_reminder.title: Smoke / CI health
smoke_or_ci_health_reminder.description: Remind which smoke tests or CI checks matter this week and how to run them locally.
smoke_or_ci_health_reminder.prompt:
From CI config and package scripts, list **smoke or health checks** worth running this week.
- For each: **command**, **expected green signal**, **when to run** (before release, daily, etc.).
- If CI files are missing, propose a **minimal** manual smoke path for this repo type.
- Do not claim CI passed without evidence.

agentSettings.cardModelsSubtitle: Chat, vision, and image generation defaults
agentSettings.cardWorkspaceSubtitle: Working directory and inbound media limits
agentSettings.cardGenerationSubtitle: Token budget, randomness, and tool loop depth

desc.modelFallbacks: Tried in order when the primary model returns an error after transient retries. Requires API keys for each provider.
desc.imageModel: Optional. Used for image understanding / vision.
desc.imageModelFallbacks: When the chat model has no vision, these vision models describe inbound images (and for the image tool). Tried in order.
desc.imageGenerationModelFallbacks: Tried in order when the primary image generation model fails (e.g. quota or provider error).
desc.mediaMaxMb: Max size when loading images in the image tool.
desc.browserEnabled: Exposes Playwright browser_* tools to the model. Install Chromium once on the gateway host: npx playwright install chromium.
desc.browserHeadless: When off, Chromium shows a window on the gateway machine (useful for debugging). When on, runs in the background.
desc.maxTokens: Maximum tokens in the model response.
desc.maxToolIterations: Maximum tool calls per user message.
desc.thinkingDefault: Default thinking level for new sessions.
desc.reasoningDefault: Whether to surface model reasoning in the chat UI. Per-session overrides (e.g. /reasoning) take precedence until cleared.
desc.verboseDefault: Agent verbosity for logs/tool detail elsewhere — not the reasoning/thinking panel. Use Reasoning visibility to hide reasoning.

advanced.cardLimitsSubtitle: Wall-clock cap per user turn, request retries, and tool failure budget.
advanced.maxTaskDurationMsDesc: Per-user-turn wall time for LLM and tools. Leave empty to use the server default. Range 1–240 min (1 min–4 h).
advanced.maxRequestsPerTurnDesc: LLM request attempts per user message (reliability; default 50).
advanced.maxToolFailuresPerTurnDesc: Consecutive tool errors before giving up (default 3).
advanced.cardCompactionSubtitle: When to compact older context to stay within the model window.
advanced.compactionEnabledDesc: When off, the runtime skips compaction (may use more context).
advanced.compactionModeDesc: default: standard strategy; safeguard: stricter heuristics when enabled.
advanced.triggerThresholdDesc: Fraction of context that triggers compaction (0.5–0.95).
advanced.minMessagesBeforeCompactDesc: Message count before compaction can run (default 10).
advanced.keepRecentMessagesDesc: Recent turns always kept near the tail (default 5).
advanced.evictionWindowDesc: Portion of history eligible for summary-first eviction (0.1–0.5).
advanced.retentionWindowDesc: Recent turns in the retention band (3–20).
advanced.cardPruningSubtitle: Trim oversized tool results before the model sees them.
advanced.pruningEnabledDesc: When off, full tool output may be sent to the model (higher cost).
advanced.maxToolResultCharsDesc: Default cap for a single tool result string (default 10000).
advanced.headKeepRatioDesc: Fraction kept from the start when pruning (0–1, default 0.3).
advanced.tailKeepRatioDesc: Fraction kept from the end (0–1, default 0.3).
advanced.cardMemorySubtitle: System memory, USER.md, and optional provider hooks.
advanced.memoryEnabledDesc: Master switch: curated memory snapshot, tool, and external prefetch (when set).
advanced.useEnhancedSystemDesc: When off, use workspace bootstrap only (no extra memory snapshot in system).
advanced.userProfileEnabledDesc: Add USER.md to the memory snapshot when present.
advanced.memoryProviderDesc: none/stub, or leave unset to omit.
advanced.injectionFrequencyDesc: How often to inject prefetched memory into the user message context.
advanced.memoryCharLimitDesc: Max chars for the curated memory snapshot (optional).
advanced.contextCadenceDesc: When using every turn: inject on turns 1, 1+N, … (min 1).
advanced.dialecticCadenceDesc: Reserved; not yet wired. Min 1 when set.
advanced.cardSessionSearchSubtitle: Model used to summarize past sessions for the session_search tool.
advanced.sessionSearchSummaryModelDesc: e.g. openai/gpt-4o-mini. Leave empty to use runtime defaults.
advanced.cardReviewSubtitle: Post-turn nudges for memory/skills. Opt-in: enable below.
advanced.reviewEnabledDesc: When on, a quiet follow-up may run after successful turns.
advanced.reviewMaxDurationMsDesc: Wall clock for the review run (30–600 s; default 120).
advanced.cardWebExtractSubtitle: Optional model and length for markdown web extraction.
advanced.webExtractModelDesc: Leave empty to use the default provider/model for extraction.
advanced.delegateEnabledDesc: When on, the agent may delegate to sub-agent runs (if supported).
advanced.executeCodeEnabledDesc: When on, the sandboxed code tool is available (if the runtime allows).
advanced.cardPromptSkillsSubtitle: Replaces the default system context when set. Skills restrict <available_skills> when non-empty.
advanced.systemPromptOverrideDesc: Optional full replacement; merged with per-agent entry (entry wins). Leave empty to clear.
advanced.skillsAllowlistDesc: If non-empty, only these skills appear in the prompt. Add one name per row.
advanced.cardToolsDisableSubtitle: Disable built-in tool names in agents.defaults (e.g. shell, web_search).
advanced.toolsDisableHint: List tool ids the default agent must not use. Per-agent tool settings in Agents still apply.
advanced.cardParamsSubtitle: Opaque key/value for extensions. Must be a JSON object.
advanced.paramsJsonDesc: e.g. {"myFlag": true}. Clear to remove params from the config file.
advanced.paramsInvalidJson: Params must be valid JSON object (e.g. empty or {}). Check syntax.

toolDescriptions.image_generate: Generate images using the configured image / image-generation model.
toolDescriptions.extensions: Expose tools registered by enabled extensions — disable to block all extension tools.

agentsSettings.skillsHint: Optional allowlist for <available_skills>. Inherit uses agents.defaults only; customize sets this agent’s skills array.
agentsSettings.channelsHint: config.bindings rows for this agent. Removing a rule updates the full bindings array on the gateway.
agentsSettings.channelsManualChannelHint: Gateway returned no channel list. Enter a channel id (e.g. telegram, webchat, gateway).
agentsSettings.channelsRefreshSessionsHint: Reload recent sessions for this channel
agentsSettings.channelsNoSessionsHint: No session history for this channel yet. Send a message or enter a custom peer id below.
agentsSettings.channelsCustomPeerHint: If set, overrides the session picker. Supports * globs; see session routing docs.
agentsSettings.cronHint: Isolated cron jobs can pin an agent id for the session key. Jobs without an agent id use the default agent and appear when that agent is selected.
agentsSettings.listSearchPlaceholder: Search by name, id, or workspace
agentsSettings.listNoAgentsYet: No agents yet. Create one to get started.
agentsSettings.personaHint: Set up your agent's identity and personality with a friendly form. For advanced editing, use Core files.
agentsSettings.personaSectionUserHint: Help your agent know you better
agentsSettings.personaNotesPlaceholder: Anything else your agent should know about you…
agentsSettings.personaMemoryNote: Your agent will automatically remember preferences you share in conversation (like favorite foods or habits). No need to add those here.
agentsSettings.footerSaveNotApplicable: Use actions in this section; the bar Save applies to Identity, Tools, Skills, and Core files.

providersSettings.subtitle: Provider API keys and OAuth. Keys you save here go to the gateway credential store.
providersSettings.intro: Search or open a group, expand a provider, paste a new key, then Save changes. OAuth opens in your browser when you choose it.
providersSettings.rotateHint: Rotating a key: expand the provider, paste the new secret, Save changes — no restart needed.
providersSettings.needToken: Save a gateway token to manage provider credentials.
providersSettings.metaMasked: Credential on file — enter a new key to replace.
providersSettings.metaWillSave: API key will be saved when you click Save changes.
providersSettings.envHint: API key is set via environment variable. Enter a new key above to override.
providersSettings.maskedStoredHint: Stored credential is not shown. Enter a new key above to replace it.
providersSettings.oauthHint: Use OAuth for secure authentication, or enter an API key manually.

modelsSettings.needToken: Save a gateway token to edit models.json.
modelsSettings.subtitle: Custom providers and models (models.json). Changes apply after save; reload picks up disk edits.
modelsSettings.emptyDesc: Add OpenAI-compatible endpoints (Ollama, LM Studio, OpenRouter, vLLM, etc.) and optional per-model overrides.
modelsSettings.addProviderSubtitle: Provider id must be unique (e.g. ollama, my-openai).
modelsSettings.apiKeyHint: Literal key, ENV name (uppercase), or shell command prefixed with !
modelsSettings.modelsEmpty: No custom models; built-in defaults apply where available.

channelsSettings.needToken: Save a gateway token to edit channel settings.
channelsSettings.subtitle: Telegram, Weixin, and Feishu inbound channels. Changes are written to the gateway config file.
channelsSettings.removeChannelConfirm: Remove {{name}} settings and clear saved credentials on the gateway? You can configure again later.
channelsSettings.telegramSubtitle: Bot token, allowlists, and optional multi-account JSON.
channelsSettings.weixinSubtitle: Sign in with WeChat via QR (browser or CLI), then enable below. Credentials stay on the gateway host.
channelsSettings.feishuSubtitle: Feishu app credentials, policies, and optional multi-account JSON.
channelsSettings.telegramTokenDesc: From BotFather. Stored in the gateway config.
channelsSettings.feishuAppIdDesc: From Feishu developer console (cli_xxx). Stored in the gateway config.
channelsSettings.feishuAppSecretDesc: From Feishu developer console. Stored in the gateway config.
channelsSettings.connectionModeDesc: websocket: Socket Mode. webhook: local HTTP server receives events.
channelsSettings.allowFromDmDesc: Comma-separated user IDs allowed to DM the bot (when policy uses allowlist).
channelsSettings.allowFromGroupsDesc: Comma-separated group chat IDs (when group policy is allowlist).
channelsSettings.multiAccountJsonDesc: Optional. Per-account botToken or tokenFile, policies, and groups. Empty {} uses the single token above only.
channelsSettings.weixinStepLogin: Use “Sign in with WeChat (QR)” below in this console, or see Channel documentation for CLI login.
channelsSettings.weixinStepEnable: Turn on Weixin below and save.
channelsSettings.weixinStepPairing: After QR login, DMs work immediately. Use allowlist DM policy only if you want to restrict who can message the bot.
channelsSettings.weixinAdvancedHint: Optional: allowlist, route tag, streaming, and per-account JSON—only if you need them.
channelsSettings.weixinAllowFromDesc: When DM policy is allowlist: comma-separated wxid / openid. Default pairing allows all contacts after QR login.
channelsSettings.weixinRouteTagDesc: Optional tag for routing; numeric or string.
channelsSettings.weixinDebugDesc: Extra logging for the Weixin channel.
channelsSettings.weixinAccountsJsonDesc: Per-account name, CDN base URL, route tag, and policies.
channelsSettings.weixinQrLoginDesc: Starts a login on the gateway. Scan with WeChat; when it succeeds, settings refresh automatically.
channelsSettings.weixinQrImageError: Could not render the QR code here. You can open the link in a new tab, or tap Regenerate to try again.
channelsSettings.weixinQrModalSubtitle: Use WeChat to scan the QR code below to connect.
channelsSettings.feishuQrModalSubtitle: Use Feishu/Lark on your phone to scan the QR code and create a new app.
channelsSettings.feishuQrScanHint: Scan this QR code with Feishu/Lark on your phone.
channelsSettings.feishuQrSetupDesc: Scan a QR code with Feishu/Lark to create an app automatically.
channelsSettings.agentRoutingHint: Maps each channel account to an agent via config `bindings`. Inbound messages use a session key for that agent.
channelsSettings.jsonObjectAccounts: Accounts must be a JSON object
channelsSettings.verificationTokenDesc: From Feishu event subscription settings (webhook mode).
channelsSettings.encryptKeyDesc: From Feishu event subscription settings (webhook mode).
channelsSettings.webhookPathDesc: Request URL path configured in Feishu event subscription.
channelsSettings.feishuToolsDesc: Enable only what you need. Each tool may require additional app scopes.

voiceSettings.needToken: Save a gateway token to edit voice settings.
voiceSettings.subtitle: Speech-to-text and text-to-speech for channels. Keys can also be set via environment variables.

stt.title: Speech-to-text (STT)
stt.description: Transcribe inbound voice using Alibaba DashScope or OpenAI Whisper.
stt.enableDesc: When on, voice messages can be transcribed for the agent.
stt.apiKeyDesc: Optional if the key is already in the environment.
stt.fallbackDesc: Try the other provider if the primary request fails.

tts.title: Text-to-speech (TTS)
tts.description: Synthesize assistant replies as audio when enabled.
tts.enableDesc: When on, TTS runs according to the trigger mode below.
tts.triggerDescAlways: Apply TTS to all assistant messages.
tts.triggerDescInbound: Only reply with voice when the user sends voice.
tts.triggerDescTagged: Only when the [[tts]] directive is used.
tts.edgeHint: Microsoft Edge TTS — no API key required.

notes.title: Note
notes.duration: Long audio is split automatically; quality depends on provider and model.
notes.envVars: Environment variables: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY (when not set in this form).

gatewaySettings.needToken: Save a gateway token to load and edit gateway options.
gatewaySettings.subtitle: HTTP API access token and listen address. Values are stored in the gateway config file.
gatewaySettings.tokenExpired: Your session token was rejected. Update the client token or fix the access token in config.
gatewaySettings.tokenPlaceholder: Token stored in config (optional if using env)
gatewaySettings.tokenHelp: Used to authenticate HTTP/WebSocket API requests. You can also set XOPC_GATEWAY_TOKEN.
gatewaySettings.listenHint: Effective after gateway restart if changed outside this UI.
gatewaySettings.authModeNone: Auth mode is set to none — token in config may be ignored.
gatewaySettings.updateChannelHint: Beta and dev receive builds earlier; stable is recommended for daily use.

heartbeatSettings.needToken: Save a gateway token to load and edit heartbeat options.
heartbeatSettings.subtitle: Periodic agent wake, optional delivery to a channel, and HEARTBEAT.md in your workspace. Stored in the gateway config file and workspace.
heartbeatSettings.triggerHint: Queues one heartbeat run (same as the timer). Skipped if HEARTBEAT.md is empty, outside active hours, or heartbeat is disabled.
heartbeatSettings.unsavedDoc: You have unsaved changes to HEARTBEAT.md.
heartbeatSettings.docHint: Tasks and reminders read by the agent on each heartbeat. Leave empty or comment-only to skip LLM calls and save tokens.
heartbeatSettings.intervalHint: Minimum 1 second. Saved to the gateway as milliseconds.
heartbeatSettings.intervalHintPreset: Quick preset or type seconds in the field.
heartbeatSettings.deliveryHint: Both channel and chat id are required to send non-silent replies somewhere. Otherwise the reply is only logged.
heartbeatSettings.promptHint: Leave empty to use the built-in default prompt.
heartbeatSettings.ackMaxChars: Max reply length before treating as silent (ackMaxChars)
heartbeatSettings.isolatedSession: Use a fresh session key each run
heartbeatSettings.isolatedSessionHint: Avoids mixing heartbeat context with the main chat session.
heartbeatSettings.activeHoursHint: Restrict heartbeats to this window. Clear to run any time.

webSearchSettings.title: Web search
webSearchSettings.subtitle: Configure region and search providers for the web_search tool. Without API keys, a built-in HTML fallback is used.
webSearchSettings.needToken: Save a gateway token to edit web search settings.
webSearchSettings.loadError: Failed to load web search settings
webSearchSettings.sectionRegionHint: Controls which zero-config HTML fallback is used when no API provider succeeds (China → Bing; otherwise DuckDuckGo).
webSearchSettings.sectionSearchHint: Providers are tried in order. Keys are stored in the gateway config file. Leave the list empty to use only the HTML fallback.
webSearchSettings.regionDesc: Auto uses your system timezone. Override if you are on a VPN or need a specific fallback.
webSearchSettings.maxResultsDesc: Used when the model does not pass a count (1–50).
webSearchSettings.apiKeyDesc: Optional for some setups. Leave masked to keep the saved value.
webSearchSettings.urlDesc: SearXNG base URL (e.g. http://localhost:8080). No trailing slash required.
webSearchSettings.keyPlaceholder: API key or env var name
webSearchSettings.footerHint: HTML fallbacks depend on third-party pages and may change. For production, use a supported search API (Brave, Tavily, Bing, or self-hosted SearXNG).

appearanceSettings.subtitle: Language, appearance, and text size for daily use. Stored in this browser only.
appearanceSettings.themeDescription: Light, dark, or follow your system setting.
appearanceSettings.fontScaleDescription: Adjust text size in chat and reading areas.
